title: Association of a Novel Pathogenic Variant (p.Ile366Asn) in the PLA2G6 Gene with Infantile Neuroaxonal Dystrophy
content: A couple presented to the office with an apparently healthy infant for a thorough clinical assessment, as they had previously lost two male children to a neurodegenerative disorder. They also reported the death of a male cousin abroad with the comparable condition. We aimed to evaluate a novel coding pathogenic variant c.1097 T>A, PLA2G6, within the affected family, previously identified in a deceased cousin, but its clinical significance remained undetermined. A 200 bp PCR product of target genome (including codon 366 of PLA2G6) was amplified followed by enzymatic digestion (MboI) and sequencing. Structural pathogenic variant analysis was performed using PyMOL 2.5.4. In RFLP analysis, the mutant-type allele produced a single-band of 200 bp, the wild-type allele manifested as two bands of 112 bp and 88 bp. The pathogenic variant was identified in nine family members, including two heterozygous couples with consanguineous marriages resulting in affected children. It was predicted to be deleterious by multiple bioinformatic tools. The substitution of nonpolar isoleucine with polar asparagine in the ankyrin domain of iPLA2 (Ile366Asn) resulted in missense pathogenic variant (ATC>AAC). A missense variant (p.Ile366Asn) in the PLA2G6 gene is associated with clinically evident infantile neuroaxonal dystrophy, transmitted in an autosomal recessive pattern, also predicted to be dysfunctional by bioinformatic analyses.
